title: Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Master's (CGRS-M)
description: The Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Master's program provides financial support to high-calibre scholars engaged in an eligible master's or, in some cases, doctoral program in Canada. Part of the harmonized Canada Research Training Awards Suite (CRTAS).
official_source: Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC)
eligibility: Canadian citizens, permanent residents, and international students
Enrolled or intending to enroll in a full-time eligible master's program at a Canadian institution
Meet the specific agency mandate (CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC)
Have not exceeded lifetime maximum of tri-agency support
eligibility_summary: Open to domestic and international students in full-time master's programs at Canadian institutions, subject to agency-specific research mandates.
benefits: Can be held at any eligible Canadian university
requirements: Application through CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC portal
Research proposal aligned with agency mandate
application_method: Apply directly to CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC online portal
selection_notes: Merit-based; evaluated by agency-specific peer review committees.
best_fit: High-calibre master's students seeking research funding across all disciplines.
notes: Replaces the former CGS-M program under the harmonized CRTAS suite. International students are eligible through all three agencies.

title: Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Doctoral (CGRS-D)
description: The Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Doctoral program recognizes and supports the next generation of outstanding innovators and researchers. Part of the harmonized Canada Research Training Awards Suite (CRTAS).
official_source: Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC)
eligibility: Canadian citizens, permanent residents, and international students
Enrolled or intending to enroll in a full-time eligible doctoral program at a Canadian institution
Meet the specific agency mandate (CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC)
Have not previously received a doctoral-level scholarship from CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC
Can apply a maximum of three times
eligibility_summary: Open to domestic and international doctoral students at Canadian institutions, with agency-specific research mandate alignment.
benefits: Eligible for affiliated fellowships and supplements
requirements: Application through CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC portal
Research proposal aligned with agency mandate
application_method: Apply directly to CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC online portal
selection_notes: Merit-based; evaluated by agency-specific peer review committees. Automatically considered for affiliated fellowships at some institutions.
best_fit: Outstanding doctoral students pursuing research careers across all disciplines.
notes: Replaces the former CGSD program under the harmonized CRTAS suite. Distinct from the Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarship.

title: Ontario Graduate Scholarship (OGS)
description: The Ontario Graduate Scholarship (OGS) is a merit-based scholarship program jointly funded by the Province of Ontario and Ontario universities. It supports outstanding graduate students in all disciplines of academic study.
application_period: University-specific internal deadlines; provincial competition annually
official_source: School of Graduate Studies, University of Toronto / Ontario Ministry of Colleges, Universities, Research Excellence and Security
eligibility: Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents, Protected Persons
International students with a valid study permit by the university deadline
Enrolled or intending to enroll full-time in an eligible master's or doctoral program at an Ontario university
Minimum A- average in last two academic years
Must not have exceeded lifetime maximum of government-funded student awards
eligibility_summary: Open to domestic and international graduate students at participating Ontario universities with strong academic records.
coverage: Living stipend: up to $15,000 per year
requirements: Apply through the participating Ontario university
Research proposal or statement of intent
application_method: Submit application to the Ontario university where you plan to hold the award
selection_notes: University-specific internal deadlines apply. Applications are first adjudicated at the university level, then forwarded to a centralized provincial competition.
best_fit: Graduate students with strong academic records seeking merit-based funding at Ontario universities.
notes: International students are eligible for a set number of awards at each university. Cannot be combined with certain other government awards beyond lifetime maximums.

title: Alberta Graduate Excellence Scholarship (AGES)
description: The Alberta Graduate Excellence Scholarship recognizes outstanding academic achievement of students pursuing graduate studies in Alberta. Funded by the Government of Alberta through the Alberta Heritage Scholarship Fund.
official_source: Alberta Student Aid / University of Alberta
eligibility: Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents, Protected Persons
International students with a valid study permit
Must be living in Alberta while studying at an Alberta post-secondary institution
Enrolled full-time in a thesis-based or course-based master's or doctoral program
Demonstrate academic excellence (typically GPA 3.3+)
eligibility_summary: Open to domestic and international graduate students enrolled at Alberta institutions who demonstrate outstanding academic achievement.
requirements: Nomination by home faculty/department (students cannot apply directly in most cases)
documents: Research proposal or explanation of program goals
application_method: Nominated by Alberta post-secondary institution faculty
Some institutions allow direct application via graduate awards portal
selection_notes: Institutions select recipients based on minimum eligibility criteria and any additional institution-specific criteria.
best_fit: Outstanding graduate students pursuing thesis-based or course-based studies at Alberta universities.
notes: A student may receive only one AGES per year. Not renewable. International students are eligible but must hold a valid study permit and be living in Alberta.

title: Quebec Merit Scholarship Program for Foreign Students (PBEEE)
description: The Merit Scholarship Program for Foreign Students (PBEEE) is funded by the Fonds de recherche du Québec (FRQ) and the Quebec Ministry of Higher Education. It aims to attract top foreign researchers and students to Quebec universities.
duration: Variable by level (Master's: up to 2 years; Doctoral: up to 4 years; Postdoc: 1 year; Short-term: up to 4 months)
application_period: University preselection: October 2025; FRQ final submission: December 2, 2025
eligibility: International students (not Canadian citizens or permanent residents)
Enrolled or intending to enroll at a Quebec university or CCTT network
Master's: no more than 3 full-time terms completed by May 1 following deadline
Doctoral: within first 9 full-time terms by May 1 following deadline
Postdoctoral: PhD obtained within 2 years before competition deadline
Short-term research: PhD obtained within 5 years before deadline
Preselected by a Quebec university, CCTT network, or China Scholarship Council
eligibility_summary: International students in research master's, PhD, postdoctoral, or short-term research programs at Quebec institutions, preselected by their host university.
benefits: Doctoral: CAD 25,000/year for first 9 sessions, then CAD 12,000/year for remaining sessions
Short-term research: CAD 3,000/month for up to 4 months
Tuition exemption from higher international tuition fees
coverage: Research stipend: CAD 20,000–35,000 per year depending on level
Tuition exemption for international differential fees
application_method: Step 1: Get preselected by Quebec host university or CCTT network
Step 2: Complete application on FRQnet portal by December 2, 2025
selection_notes: Two-stage process: university/CCTT preselection, then FRQ evaluation by multidisciplinary committees based on academic excellence and research potential.
best_fit: Outstanding international graduate students and researchers pursuing studies at Quebec universities.
notes: Cannot be combined with Canadian federal or Quebec government scholarships, but can be combined with private or home-country funding. Must reside in Quebec during funded studies.

title: Canada Postdoctoral Research Award (CPRA)
description: The Canada Postdoctoral Research Award program is a federal research talent investment program in the Canada Research Training Awards Suite (CRTAS), jointly administered by CIHR, NSERC, and SSHRC. It replaces the former Banting Postdoctoral Fellowships and agency-specific postdoctoral fellowships.
deadline_display: CIHR: September 16, 2026; NSERC: October 17, 2026; SSHRC: September 10, 2026
official_source: Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC)
eligibility: Canadian citizens, permanent residents, and international applicants
Hold (or expect to hold) a doctorate or health professional degree before award start date
Not hold or be on leave from a tenure-track or tenured faculty position
Have completed all degree requirements no more than three years before September 1, 2026
Cannot have previously received a tri-agency postdoctoral award
Cannot hold a CPRA concurrently with another tri-agency research training award
Apply to only one agency per year (CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC)
eligibility_summary: Outstanding postdoctoral researchers of all nationalities who have completed their PhD within the last three years and are not in tenured faculty positions.
requirements: Apply to the agency aligned with research subject (CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC)
Research proposal significantly distinct from doctoral thesis
application_method: Apply directly to CIHR ResearchNET, NSERC Online System, or SSHRC Application Portal
selection_notes: Evaluated based on research proposal quality, significance of contributions, and suitability of proposed research environment. Some awards reserved for Black postdoctoral researchers who self-identify.
best_fit: Top-tier postdoctoral researchers seeking advanced research training in Canada.
notes: Replaces the Banting Postdoctoral Fellowships and former CIHR/NSERC/SSHRC postdoctoral fellowships. Maximum three lifetime applications permitted.

title: Canada-ASEAN Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development (SEED-2)
description: The Canada-ASEAN Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development (SEED-2) program offers short-term study or research opportunities in Canada for students from ASEAN member states and, under SEED-2, Pacific Island Countries and Mongolia. Funded by Global Affairs Canada under Canada's Indo-Pacific Strategy.
application_period: Applications open January 2026; institutional deadline March 24, 2026
eligibility: Citizens of ASEAN member states (Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam) or SEED-2 eligible Pacific Island Countries and Mongolia
Enrolled full-time at a post-secondary institution in home country
Continue paying tuition to home institution during exchange
Undergraduate/college: valid student exchange agreement between home and Canadian institutions
Graduate: supervisor invitation letter from Canadian host institution
No Canadian citizenship or permanent residency
Not already studying in Canada
Must not have previously received a SEED scholarship
eligibility_summary: Full-time students from eligible ASEAN/Pacific/Mongolia institutions for short-term study or research exchanges at Canadian designated learning institutions.
benefits: Host institution receives CAD 500 per scholar
coverage: Tuition waived by Canadian host institution
requirements: Letter of intent (maximum 1 page) aligned with UN Sustainable Development Goals
Letter of support from home institution
documents: Letter of support from home university
application_method: Students cannot apply directly. Canadian host institution's international office submits application via MyEduCanada portal.
selection_notes: Global Affairs Canada reviews applications based on alignment with Sustainable Development Goals, research merit, and institutional partnerships.
best_fit: Students from eligible Indo-Pacific countries seeking short-term academic or research exchanges at Canadian universities.
notes: Non-deferrable and non-renewable. Students must return to home institution after exchange. Tuition is waived by the Canadian host institution.

title: Schulich Leader Scholarships
description: Schulich Leader Scholarships are Canada's most coveted undergraduate STEM scholarships. One hundred scholarships are awarded annually to entrepreneurial-minded high school graduates enrolling in STEM programs at 20 partner universities across Canada.
application_period: Nomination deadline: January 28, 2026; Application deadline: February 18, 2026
eligibility: Graduating high school or cégep in Canada in the 2026/2027 academic year
Canadian citizen
Plan to enroll in an eligible STEM program at a partner university
Entrepreneurial-minded (exhibiting leadership, charisma, and creativity)
Strong consideration given to students with financial need
Intend to pursue a career in Technology, Engineering, Entrepreneurship and business enterprise, or Applied scientific research
eligibility_summary: Canadian citizens graduating from Canadian high schools or CEGEPs who plan to study STEM at one of 20 partner universities.
requirements: Nomination by high school guidance counsellor (one per school per year, or four per CEGEP)
Academic achievement implied by university admission
documents: List of top three achievements (50 words each)
application_method: Step 1: Get nominated by high school guidance counsellor by January 28, 2026
Step 2: Submit online scholarship application by February 18, 2026
selection_notes: Highly competitive; evaluated on academic excellence, leadership, entrepreneurial spirit, and financial need.
best_fit: Outstanding Canadian high school graduates with leadership and entrepreneurial potential in STEM fields.
notes: Not considering students who focus on activism
